verdict.rationale: Make documents a broad, resource-oriented REST API (v2, described by an OpenAPI 3.0 spec) covering connections and their access lists, data stores, AI agents, audit logs, analytics, custom properties and on-prem agents. Its MCP server also lets AI clients run scenarios and manage account contents. However, nothing states or demonstrates that every UI action is available programmatically, and some surfaces are limited: AI Agents endpoints are in open beta and analytics is Enterprise-only. Missing for 10: an explicit UI–API parity claim or coverage map, evidence that scenario building and editing is fully exposed via the REST API, independent hands-on corroboration of parity, and a stability or deprecation policy.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Make API follows the REST API design. Make API is organized into resource-oriented URLs
The following endpoints allow you to get, create, update, delete, and run AI Agents. These endpoints are available in **open beta** to all users.
The following endpoints let you view and manage the access list (entity ACL) of a connection
View and modify scenarios and their related entities (e.g., connections, webhooks, and data stores)
Make MCP server allows AI systems, such as large language models (LLMs), to run scenarios and manage the contents of your Make account.
